settingText: Present-day Pax-Aeterna treaty vault, preserved as a ceremonial ruin whose official history describes negotiations nobody can name.
summary: Theo, Rae and Adrian enter Pax-Aeterna looking for the source of a shared recurring image: an empty chair at a black table. The room remembers before any of them touch it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Present-day Pax-Aeterna treaty vault in ordinary civic quiet: worn stone, museum barriers, modest explanatory plaques with names and events missing, daylight falling across a black treaty table and one empty chair. Theo, Rae and Adrian enter without spectacle.
Panel 2 — Theo stops at the empty chair: 'I've seen that chair.' Rae, already staring at it: 'So have I.' Their recognition is simultaneous and unwelcome.

Panel 3 — Adrian: 'Then we should leave.' Rae turns on him: 'You knew we'd say that.' His fear confirms the room matters. Adrian: 'I hoped you wouldn't.' Hold on the three present-day faces and the ordinary room; no device activates and nobody touches the table.

Panel 4 — Match transition. The same black table fills the frame as present-day museum ropes and quiet light give way to the ancient chamber's open doors, evacuation noise and living occupants. Theo and Rae are not visible anywhere in the ancient frame.

summary: Mero prepares for a negotiation nobody believes will hold. Atlas demands that evacuation continue regardless of any agreement; Redlin insists a ceasefire is still worth attempting even if Starbreaker distrusts it.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Ancient treaty chamber. The black stone table is functional, not royal; broad doors open directly onto a city evacuating below. Mero, Atlas and Redlin prepare while transport queues remain visible in the background. No ancient Theo or Rae appears. Atlas, monumental but focused on the evacuation beyond the doors: 'The ships leave whether they sign or not.' Redlin: 'Agreed.'

Panel 2 — Mero, dryly: 'That was easy.' Redlin: 'Don't get used to it.' Atlas almost smiles; Redlin gives Mero a tired sideways look while transport crews continue working beyond the open doors. Atlas: 'I'm serious.' He points not to a tactical display but to actual transports and civilians moving outside.

Panel 3 — Mero: 'So am I. That's why I'm grateful for the easy part.' End in a wide panel with Mero, Atlas and Redlin together at the overlook while an evacuation ship lifts away below them, its light crossing all three faces.

dialogueInline.text: The ships leave whether they sign or not.
So am I. That's why I'm grateful for the easy part.

SETTING STATE — Ancient Pax-Aeterna treaty chamber before a final negotiation, black stone table, open doors to a city under evacuation.

summary: Arbiter debuts as a person carrying responsibility rather than a cold embodiment of judgment. Arbiter already knows the evacuation agreement and asks who will own the decision if evacuation fails.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Arbiter enters alone in pale/dark judicial armor with restrained gold structure. Her shoulders are slightly rounded under the armor, one gauntlet carries a worn physical case and her face shows fatigue; Mero, Atlas and Redlin turn toward her.
Panel 2 — Arbiter looks through the open doors at evacuation ships: 'Who decided they had time?' Atlas immediately: 'I did.'
Panel 3 — Arbiter: 'Good.' Atlas: 'You sound disappointed.' Her attention remains on him as a person who owns a promise, not an opponent.

Panel 4 — Arbiter: 'No. I prefer when the person making a promise stays in the room.' Atlas stops pacing and squares his feet beside the table; Arbiter keeps her eyes on him until he gives a small nod.

Panel 5 — Mero: 'We're all staying.' Arbiter: 'Until one of us decides someone else can't.' End with the empty chair visible at the table, turning the present-day recurring image into an unresolved ancient absence.

dialogueInline.text: No. I prefer when the person making a promise stays in the room.
Until one of us decides someone else can't.

settingText: Ancient side chamber overlooking evacuation streets below Pax-Aeterna.
summary: Atlas confronts Arbiter privately over the possibility of sacrificing the threatened system. Arbiter refuses to pretend that refusing sacrifice means no one will die.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Atlas and Arbiter stand in a side chamber overlooking real evacuation streets below: families carrying bags, medical transports, packed departure lanes. Both can see individual people. No ancient Theo or Rae appears.

Panel 2 — Atlas: 'You came here prepared to kill a world.' Keep his enormous body turned toward the civilians, not squaring off like a fighter. Arbiter: 'I came prepared to admit that might be the choice.' She keeps both hands flat on the stone sill and looks down at the evacuation lanes while she says it; her face remains tense and tired.
Panel 3 — 'That's not courage.' / 'Refusing the order doesn't make the danger go away.' Their philosophies collide while both continue watching the same people below.

Panel 4 — Atlas: 'There are people down there.' Arbiter: 'There are people everywhere this reaches.' End on evacuation craft disappearing toward distant populated systems, visually making both scopes of responsibility real.

dialogueInline.text: You came here prepared to kill a world.
I came prepared to admit that might be the choice.
Refusing the order doesn't make the danger go away.
There are people everywhere this reaches.

summary: Starbreaker arrives and immediately distrusts the ceasefire. Redlin accuses him of wanting the negotiation to fail; Starbreaker accuses Redlin of treating every pause as evidence that peace is possible.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Starbreaker arrives through the open chamber doors, white-gold fractured armor worn and dulled, while evacuation alarms and moving civilians remain visible behind him. No ancient Theo or Rae appears.
Panel 2 — Redlin: 'Try not to end the meeting before it starts.' Starbreaker: 'Try not to call a delay peace.' Their exchange lands like an old argument they can both recite.
Panel 3 — Mero, exhausted: 'I missed both of you.' Starbreaker and Redlin both glance at him; Redlin gives the smallest involuntary half-smile before Arbiter answers.
Panel 4 — Arbiter, dry: 'No, you didn't.' Mero looks at her, caught.
Panel 5 — Mero: 'No. I really didn't.' A brief rueful look passes between Mero, Redlin and Starbreaker, then all three turn toward the worsening alarm and the civilians moving beyond the doors.

dialogueInline.text: Try not to end the meeting before it starts.
Try not to call a delay peace.

summary: The ceasefire begins failing through human consequences: routes close, ships turn back and separated families run out of time.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Public gallery as the ceasefire visibly fails: one departure gate closes while a family reaches it from opposite sides.
Panel 2 — A transport reverses course and civilians press toward shrinking routes; the human consequences remain visible in the same space as the principals.
Panel 3 — Mero and the champions see the failure directly rather than through a tactical display.
Panel 4 — Hold on separated civilians and stalled transport crews; no ancient Theo or Rae appears.
Panel 5 — Starbreaker: 'Now.' Redlin: 'Not with the transports still inside.' Frame them against those transports.
Panel 6 — Atlas: 'Then we keep the transports moving.' Arbiter: 'They will not all leave.' A damaged departure lane makes both statements physically plausible.

dialogueInline.text: Not with the transports still inside.
Then we keep the transports moving.

summary: The principals fall back onto their characteristic answers while the negotiation collapses around civilians.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Mero says, 'I know,' while looking toward the damaged passage and the people still trapped there.
Panel 2 — Atlas turns on him immediately and steps close enough to force eye contact.
Panel 3 — Atlas says, 'Don't say it like that.' Civilians remain visible behind him.
Panel 4 — Mero holds Atlas's stare while evacuation workers try to clear the blocked route between them.
Panel 5 — Tight on Mero's exhausted human face, soot and sleeplessness visible.
Panel 6 — Reverse toward Atlas with trapped civilians blurred over his shoulder; neither man has a better phrase for what is happening.
Panel 7 — Mero asks, 'How would you like me to say it?'

settingText: Ancient empty corridor behind the treaty chamber while the larger crisis continues outside.
summary: Mero asks Arbiter whether they can live with the extinction decision. Arbiter says living with it is not the same as being entitled to make it, but someone will make a choice either by acting or refusing to act.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Mero and Arbiter step into a nearly empty service corridor behind the treaty chamber. Evacuation noise continues through open doorways, keeping the private conversation attached to public suffering. No ancient Theo or Rae appears.

Panel 2 — Mero steps close to Arbiter and lowers his voice: 'Can you live with it?' His command posture is gone; one hand rests heavily on the table, fingers spread, while he waits at eye level for her face to answer.
Panel 3 — Arbiter: 'That is not the standard.' Mero: 'It should be somewhere on the list.' Arbiter's eyes drop to his exhausted hand on the table, then return to his face before she answers.

Panel 4 — Arbiter: 'If I give the order, those deaths are mine. If I refuse and this spreads, those deaths are mine too.' No judicial pose; the burden is personal. Mero: 'You make that sound honest.' Arbiter: 'It is only honest.' End with them turning back toward the chamber without absolution. The decision remains theirs to make.

dialogueInline.text: It should be somewhere on the list.
If I give the order, those deaths are mine. If I refuse and this spreads, those deaths are mine too.

settingText: Ancient evacuation concourse at Pax-Aeterna, civilians waiting beneath an increasingly impossible sky.
summary: Atlas, Redlin and Starbreaker work together to move civilians even while arguing about the larger decision. The scene prevents ideology from erasing shared action: enemies in principle can still carry the same injured person.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Evacuation concourse under an impossible sky. Atlas lifts a collapsed barrier, Redlin supports an injured civilian under one arm and Starbreaker carries two heavy baggage cases while moving with the crowd.
Panel 2 — No ancient Theo or Rae appears.
Panel 3 — Atlas takes one side of an injured civilian: 'Take his other arm.' Starbreaker immediately: 'I have him.' Their hands meet under the person's weight.

Panel 4 — Redlin clears fallen material from the route and says, 'For once, nobody argue with Atlas.' Atlas immediately takes the opened side of the transport while Starbreaker braces the opposite frame; all three work on the same damaged vehicle.
Panel 5 — Starbreaker: 'Enjoy it.' Redlin: 'I am.' Brief shared humor survives inside the evacuation.
Panel 6 — Large final panel. The three ideological opponents carry the same injured stranger toward safety as the sky worsens behind them. End on shared action surviving political rupture.

dialogueInline.text: For once, nobody argue with Atlas.

summary: The final evacuation limit arrives. Arbiter begins the irreversible decision in a room where no clean option remains.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Return to the treaty chamber after the evacuation has visibly reached its limit. Through the doors: departure gates closing, people holding one another, a last transport loading.
Panel 2 — No countdown or abstract display. No ancient Theo or Rae appears.
Panel 3 — Arbiter: 'I am ending it here.' Hold the entire group in frame so the decision lands between people who know one another.
Panel 4 — Atlas: 'No.' Arbiter: 'I know.' Arbiter looks at Atlas for a long beat, then turns back to the decision sheet without asking him to agree.

Panel 3 — Starbreaker says, 'Don't call this clean afterward.' Mero answers, 'No one will.'
Panel 4 — Hold on Mero not stopping Arbiter while the final door remains visible in the background.

summary: Atlas remains with Arbiter after everyone else leaves. He tells Arbiter that taking responsibility does not make the act right. Arbiter agrees. Their disagreement survives without either receiving absolution.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Empty treaty chamber after everyone else has gone. The black table, scattered personal objects and open doors remain; evacuation noise has receded. Atlas and Arbiter stand far apart in the same human-scale room. No ancient Theo or Rae appears.

Panel 2 — Atlas: 'You don't get credit for admitting it now.' His anger has collapsed into grief. Arbiter: 'I didn't.' No defense, no triumph, no attempt to justify herself beyond ownership. Atlas: 'Then what do you call this?' Hold the empty chair in the composition between them.

Panel 3 — Tight final ancient panel on Arbiter: 'Mine.' Arbiter keeps his eyes on the empty chair and does not ask Atlas for forgiveness. End the ancient chapter here without showing the unseen aides whose identities remain suppressed.

summary: Theo asks the question Adrian has been avoiding: were they physically there? Adrian finally says yes.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Present-day outer steps at dusk. Ordinary city life continues below while Theo, Rae and Adrian stand apart from it, emotionally exhausted. No memory imagery or ancient doubles appear.
Panel 2 — Theo: 'Were we there?' Adrian: 'Yes.' Rae immediately: 'Where?' Keep Adrian's answer plain, not theatrical.
Panel 3 — Adrian faces Rae across the black table: 'You sat beside Arbiter.' Rae says, 'No.' Adrian answers, 'You recorded the rulings.'
Panel 4 — Hold on present-day Rae as her grip tightens on the chair back and she stops breathing for a beat.

summary: Adrian reveals that Rae served beside Arbiter and Theo served Mero. The mystery becomes their own participation.

panelPlan.text: Panel 1 — Theo: 'And me?' Adrian: 'Mero's staff. Junior attaché.' Theo: 'Why haven't we seen ourselves?' The reveal is identity continuity, not reincarnation or possession.
Panel 2 — Adrian: 'Because that was the last thing the Reset took.' Rae: 'What did we do?' Adrian: 'That's what I'm afraid you'll remember next.'
Panel 3 — End on Theo and Rae standing shoulder-width apart at the black table, both staring at Adrian; keep only their present-day bodies in frame.
